publication.eligibility_criteria:
the focus of the the paper is not primarily on automated
software testing
• topic is teaching-specific
• not software testing, e.g., system, hardware, deployment
configuration
• manual testing
• model checking and symbolic execution
• optimisation or prioritisation (of testing execution)
• in-line code assertions instead of test cases
• test data generation (test case generation and assertion generation were included)
• experience report with no qualitative or quantitative analysis
• not software (e.g., testing in a manufacturing context)
• not reporting results properly (i.e. not following commonly
accepted guidelines [42])
• behind a paywall (typically other than ACM, IEEE, Springer,
Elsevier, Wiley)
• not written in English
selecting papers from the
MS pool that met any of the following inclusion criteria:
• papers that mine data from existing software repositories to
understand practices used
• surveys, interviews and focus groups used to understand
industry practices
• empirical studies with industrial applications
• techniques proposed or discussed by industry
• academic case studies or experiments in which industry
representatives participated
